Estimate species geographic ranges from occurrence records

Source: R/lets_range.R
lets.range.Rd

Constructs geographic range polygons from species occurrence records using spatial clustering followed by buffered concave hulls. Occurrence records are first grouped into spatial clusters based on pairwise geographic distances. A concave hull is then generated for each cluster and spatially restricted using a user-defined `sf` object.

Usage

lets.range(
  occs,
  n_max = 1000,
  eps_m = 1e+06,
  min_pts = 1,
  ratio = 0.5,
  buf = 50000,
  crop_shp,
  round_par = 3,
  plot_map = TRUE,
  intersection = TRUE
)

Arguments

occs

A data frame containing species occurrence records. It must include the columns `scientificName`, `decimalLongitude`, and `decimalLatitude`.

n_max

Integer. Maximum number of occurrence records retained for each species. Species with more records are randomly subsampled. Default is `1000`.

eps_m

Numeric. Maximum distance, in meters, used by DBSCAN to define spatial clusters. Default is `1000000` meters (1000 km).

min_pts

Integer. Minimum number of points required to form a DBSCAN cluster. Default is `1`.

ratio

Numeric between 0 and 1 controlling the concavity of the hull. A value of `1` produces a convex hull, whereas values approaching `0` produce increasingly concave hulls. Default is `0.5`.

buf

Numeric. Buffer distance, in meters, applied before and after construction of the concave hull. Default is `50000`.

crop_shp

An `sf` object defining the spatial feature used to restrict the estimated range polygons. Its effect depends on `intersection`. When `intersection = TRUE`, only the portion of the estimated range overlapping `crop_shp` is retained. When `intersection = FALSE`, the portion overlapping `crop_shp` is removed.

round_par

Integer. Number of decimal places used to round geographic coordinates before removing duplicated records. Default is `3`.

plot_map

Logical. If `TRUE`, plots `crop_shp`, the resulting range polygons, and the occurrence records for each species. Default is `TRUE`.

intersection

Logical. Determines how `crop_shp` is applied to the estimated range polygons. If `TRUE`, [sf::st_intersection()] is used and only areas overlapping `crop_shp` are retained. If `FALSE`, [sf::st_difference()] is used and areas overlapping `crop_shp` are removed. Default is `TRUE`.

Value

An `sf` object containing the estimated geographic range polygons for all species in EPSG:4326, with `binomial` and integer `cluster` columns. Each surviving cluster occupies one MULTIPOLYGON row. When no polygons survive, an empty `sf` with the same columns and CRS is returned.

Details

For each species, coordinates are rounded according to `round_par` and duplicated records are removed. If the number of unique occurrence records exceeds `n_max`, a random subset of records is retained.

Pairwise geographic distances among occurrence records are calculated using [lets.distmat()]. Records are then grouped into spatial clusters using [dbscan::dbscan()]. A buffered concave hull is constructed independently for each cluster using [sf::st_concave_hull()]. DBSCAN noise (label 0) is omitted. Buffers before and after the hull are computed in a local azimuthal equidistant projection centered using the circular mean longitude. This is a regional range estimator; metric distortion increases for clusters extending far from their center. With the default `min_pts = 1` and positive `buf`, even one unique occurrence produces a buffered polygon (approximately `2 * buf` radius before masking). Two-point and collinear clusters are also supported. Repeated records at one location count as one occurrence after rounding. Higher `min_pts` still applies: isolated points classified as noise are omitted, and a mask can remove the entire buffered range. With `buf = 0`, clusters with no polygonal area are omitted.

Ranges and masks are split at the antimeridian before Cartesian overlays on their longitude/latitude coordinates. These overlays follow the mapped edges of the mask, rather than interpreting them as S2 great-circle arcs. No distance or buffer is calculated in degrees, and the caller's S2 setting is unchanged. Missing species and invalid coordinates are dropped with a warning; `crop_shp` must have a known CRS.

The resulting polygons are subsequently combined with `crop_shp`. When `intersection = TRUE`, only the portion overlapping `crop_shp` is retained. This can be used, for example, to restrict terrestrial species ranges to land areas. When `intersection = FALSE`, the portion overlapping `crop_shp` is removed. This can be used to remove land polygons from the ranges of marine species.

The choice of `eps_m`, `ratio`, and `buf` can substantially influence the resulting range geometry and should reflect the spatial scale, sampling properties, and biological characteristics of the study system.

Note that the function requires sf >= 1.0-11 and GEOS >= 3.11.0 for concave hull construction.

See also

[lets.distmat()], [dbscan::dbscan()], [sf::st_concave_hull()], [sf::st_intersection()], [sf::st_difference()]

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(sf)
library(rnaturalearth)

# Example occurrence records for a marine species
occs <- data.frame(
  scientificName = "Example_brasiliensis",
  decimalLongitude = c(-38.2, -37.8, -36.8, -35.5, -34.8) + 1,
  decimalLatitude = c(-23, -22, -10.5, -8.5, -7)
)

# Land polygons used to remove terrestrial areas
land <- ne_countries(
  scale = "medium",
  returnclass = "sf"
)

# Estimate a marine range by removing land from the range polygons
ranges <- lets.range(
  occs,
  crop_shp = land,
  intersection = FALSE,
  buf = 100000,
  eps_m = 1000000, 
  ratio = 1
)
} # }
